title: Toddler shawl in double crochet
subtitle: A 75 cm square in DK-weight double crochet for ages 2 to 4, worked flat with no shaping
excerpt: This toddler shawl is a 75 cm square of double crochet in DK yarn on a 4 mm hook, sized for ages 2 to 4. The construction is entirely plain double crochet with no shaping. The square folds diagonally and is worn as a triangle draped over small shoulders. It is the most structurally direct entry point for double crochet on a usable project.
heroPrompt: A small crochet square shawl in soft pale yellow DK yarn folded into a triangle and laid flat on a wooden nursery shelf with a soft toy beside it, photographed in natural light.

glossaryTerms.definition: The UK term for the move US patterns call single crochet (sc). Insert hook, pull up loop (2 loops on hook), yarn over, pull through both loops. Short, dense stitch that produces a firm fabric.

A chain worked at the beginning of a row to bring the yarn up to the height of the first stitch. In double crochet, the turning chain is ch 1 and does not count as a stitch. You work the first dc into the very first stitch of the row below.

content.text: This is a 75 cm square of
double crochet (dc)

in DK yarn on a 4 mm hook. The square has no shaping: every row is the same. Once finished, fold it diagonally and drape it over a toddler's shoulders. The only technique required is dc and managing the
turning chain
correctly at the start of each row.

The turning chain in double crochet is ch 1 and does not count as a stitch. This means the first dc of each row goes into the first actual stitch of the previous row, not into the turning chain. Getting this right from row 1 keeps the stitch count stable across all 165 rows.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 250 g DK-weight yarn in a soft fibre suitable for a child (cotton, cotton-blend, or machine-washable treated wool). A 4 mm crochet hook (US G/6). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

18 dc x 22 rows = 10 x 10 cm in DK yarn with a 4 mm hook, measured unstretched. Work a 15 x 15 cm swatch, measure the central 10 cm in each direction, and adjust hook size before starting. One stitch per 10 cm off changes the finished square from 75 cm by about 4 cm.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc): UK; the same move as US "single crochet" (sc).
Pattern
The shawl is worked flat. The foundation chain is one side of the square. Every row is identical. The stitch count stays at 135 dc throughout.
Foundation chain
Ch 136. (This gives 135 working stitches, which measures 75 cm at the stated gauge.)
Row 1 (right side)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch throughout). 1 dc in each ch across. Turn. (135 sts)
Row 2 onwards
Ch 1 (does not count as stitch). 1 dc in the first st (not the turning chain). 1 dc in each st across to end. Turn. (135 sts)

Check the stitch count at the end of every 10th row while you are learning the pattern. Count the tops of the stitches along the row just completed. You should have 135 every time. A count of 134 means you missed the first stitch; a count of 136 means you worked into the turning chain by mistake.
Continue to row 165
Continue repeating row 2 until the piece measures 75 cm from the foundation chain edge, approximately 165 rows at 22 rows per 10 cm. Fasten off. (135 sts)
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in both ends securely. Thread the tail through the backs of stitches in different directions for at least 5 cm. A single row of dc worked around all four edges with a contrast colour gives a neat frame and hides the foundation chain edge. Wet-block to 75 x 75 cm if the square is not lying flat.
Care
Machine-wash at 30 degrees on a gentle cycle if the yarn is machine-washable. Otherwise handwash in cool water with mild soap. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next

Work the same square construction with a stripe sequence: change colour every 8 rows. A crochet border of shell stitch worked into the selvedge stitches turns the plain square into a mini heirloom piece. For a larger size (ages 4 to 6), increase the foundation chain to 162 and work 198 rows to produce a 90 cm square.
